criteria.q: Senior Housing Offset (8 Points)
criteria.note: Eight points for projects primarily housing senior households, but none if income-restricted funding encumbers more than 20% of the units. This is the item that accounts for the Section 3 gap: the nine items sum to 46 and the section maximum is 38, a difference of exactly 8. The plan states no rule making the offset exclusive of anything. Its 20% restriction ceiling does limit 3.a in practice: a project with at most 20% restricted units can score at most 2.4 there. That looks like the intent of the name, compensating senior projects that cannot earn the income-targeting points, but it is an inference. tracks.note: Section 7.1.1, p.24: 'The maximum number of points is 97.' MISMATCH, recorded not resolved. The stated section maxima of 7.3 (69) and 7.4 (30) sum to 99 before 7.2's project type priority points. The computed 115 is 99 + 15 (7.2 at its largest value, Tribal Housing) + 1 (7.2.7 veterans preference). A non-Tribal project's ceiling is 110 (99 + 10 + 1); a Tribal project's is 107, because Tribal projects are barred from the 8 amenity points (99 - 8 + 15 + 1). Neither equals 97, and 97 is not reachable by dropping any whole section: excluding all of 7.2 still leaves 99. The gap matters beyond bookkeeping, because p.6 requires applications to 'earn at least 60% of the available points', and 60% of 97 is 58.2 while 60% of 110 is 66. A reviewer should confirm the 97 against p.24 and each section maximum against pp.26-36.

Section 8.2, pp.37-38: 'Total Available 40'. These are additional points on top of a base of 60 that every project receives once it meets the Section 6 pre-application thresholds: 'All projects will start with 60 points ... Additional points will be capped at 40, for a maximum total score of 100 points.' The base is not coded as a criterion because nothing is scored to earn it. The five criteria sum to exactly 40. criteria.note: CONTRADICTION, recorded not resolved: the rule is '3 points per 1% in waivers and/or contributions', which reaches 35 at about 11.7% of project costs, but the document's own example gives a 10% reduction 35 points, where the rule gives 30. Non-federal contributions from unrelated parties only; deferred developer fee does not count.

criteria.q: Total Project Costs (Up to a negative 1000 points)
criteria.note: -10 per 1% over the Attachment A total project cost limits, up to -1000: large enough to eliminate any application. WCDA may waive all negative points for one over-limit project a round and offer a pro-rated award under the Statistical Outlier Method (p.50).
